To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lbc protooncogene encodes a guanine nucleotidetransferase that is a Rho-specific exchange factor.

the proto-oncogene lbc encodes a protein that specifically activates the small GTP binding Rho protein, and that the proto-lbc protein has an extended C terminus that regulates its transforming activity and subcellular localization.

the lbc proto- and oncoprotein differ in their C termini, and that the proto-Lbc α-helical, proline-rich region, and the PH domain are necessary for full Lbc transforming activity, but not for Lbc localization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanisms of transformation of the Lbc proto-oncogenes.
the mechanism of activation of Rho GTPase by Lbc, and the regulation of the Lbc oncogene product by its C terminus.
the mechanism of activation of the Rho GTPase, and the role of this activation in cell transformation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proto-lbc C terminus is a novel, important regulator of Lbc function and that the C terminally truncated onco-Lbc is an aberrant product that is constitutively active in the cytoplasm, and thus capable of transformation.
the Lbc RndGEF is a novel RhoGEF, that is, an oncogenic protein that can activate Rho GTPase and promote cell growth and proliferation.
while the DH domain of Lbc is essential for Rho activation, the PH domain is essential for Lbc transformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proto-Lbc product is an Rho exchange factor that is regulated by a C terminus that includes a novel α-helical cyto-matrix protein domain that may be involved in targeting proto-Lbc, and that the onco-Lb product is a truncated, deregulated form of the proto-Lb product that is constitutively localized to the cytoplasm.

the Lbc RHOGEF proto-oncogene is regulated by a novel C termini, which is absent from the onco-LBC product, and which is responsible for regulating both the subcellular localization and the transforming activity of the protein.

the lbc proto- and oncoproteins are both capable of promoting Rho activation, but the C terminus of the proto-protein is required for optimal activity and that this region also plays a role in regulating the subcellular distribution of the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proto-Lbc product, which is a guanine exchange factor for the Rho small guanosine triphosphate binding protein, is regulated by its C terminus.
the C termini of the proto-oncogene product and the onco-protein are different.
the proto-oncogene lbc is a Rho exchange factor that can be activated by truncation of a C-terminal sequence that includes a predicted alpha-helical region and proline-rich domain.
